For every \(i\in[H]\), let \(K\) and \(K'\) satisfy \(K_t(y_t\mid x_t)\ge\kappa\) and \(K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)\ge\kappa\) for every \(t\in[H]\). Then
\[
 \max\!\left\{|L_i(K,\tau)-L_i(K',\tau)|,
                 |U_i(K,\tau)-U_i(K',\tau)|\right\}
 \le \frac{4DH}{\kappa}\,\delta(K,K').
\]
Define the certified positivity-preserving radius by \(r_{\mathrm{pos}}(\kappa)=\kappa/2\). If only \(K_t(y_t\mid x_t)\ge\kappa\) is initially known and \(\delta(K,K')<r_{\mathrm{pos}}(\kappa)\), then \(K'_t(y_t\mid x_t)>\kappa/2\) for every \(t\), and, for each \(E_i\in\{L_i,U_i\}\),
\[
 E_i(K,\tau)-\frac{8DH}{\kappa}\delta(K,K')
 \le E_i(K',\tau)
 \le E_i(K,\tau)+\frac{8DH}{\kappa}\delta(K,K').
\]
On the coverage event \(K\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)\), let
\[
 r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)
 =\sup_{K'\in\mathcal C_{1-\alpha}(\widehat K)}\delta(K,K').
\]
If \(K_t(y_t\mid x_t)\ge\kappa\) for every \(t\) and \(r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)<\kappa/2\), then
\[
 L_i(K,\tau)-\frac{8DH}{\kappa}r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)
 \le L_i^{\alpha}\le L_i(K,\tau)
\]
and
\[
 U_i(K,\tau)
 \le U_i^{\alpha}
 \le U_i(K,\tau)+\frac{8DH}{\kappa}r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K).
\]
Consequently, the plug-in endpoints are uniformly consistent on classes with \(\kappa\)-positive factual cells whenever \(\delta(\widehat K,K)\) converges uniformly to zero in probability. The displayed confidence-fiber brackets also give uniform convergence on any sequence of coverage events for which \(r_{\mathcal C}(K,\widehat K)\) converges uniformly to zero.

 \qquad y\in\mathcal S.
 \tag{1}

\[

 \left\{v\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal S}:0\le v(y)\le u_{t,x}(y),\ 
              \sum_{y\in\mathcal S}v(y)=1\right\}.
 \tag{2}
\]

Conversely, in a convex decomposition of a point with all but at most one coordinate at a bound, every bound coordinate agrees in the two summands, and the sum-to-one constraint fixes the remaining coordinate.

These moves traverse every edge because an edge of the box intersected with the sum hyperplane can free at most two box constraints.  To verify reachability, fix any target vertex \(v^\star\). At any other vertex, \(v^\star-v\) decomposes into transfers from decreasing to increasing coordinates; when \(v\) has a unique non-bound coordinate, a transfer between two bound coordinates can be split through that coordinate.  At least one locally feasible transfer strictly increases the functional.  Maximal movement reaches another vertex, and finiteness forces a path to \(v^\star\). \[

 \tag{3}
\]

\[

 \qquad
 \eta_{jb}=\begin{cases}+,&a_{jb}^\sigma\ge0,\\-,&a_{jb}^\sigma<0.\end{cases}
 \tag{4}
\]
Because \(|a_{j0}^\sigma|=|a_{j1}^\sigma|=|\nu_j|\), \(\sum_{j,b}\rho_{jb}=1\).  Introduce one global chance variable \(W\) with alphabet \([H]\times\{0,1\}\times[H]\) and law
\[
 \Pr\{W=(j,b,\ell)\}=\frac{\rho_{jb}}{H}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Conditional on its first two coordinates, use at time \(t\) the action kernel
\[
 \gamma_t^{jb}(a\mid s)=
 \begin{cases}
  \alpha_i^b(a\mid s),&t=i,\\
  (1-\zeta_j)\alpha_t^0(a\mid s)+\zeta_j\alpha_t^1(a\mid s),&t\ne i.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{6}
\]

\[
 \psi_{t,x}(S_t,A_t,S_{t+1},Z_{t,x})=
 \begin{cases}
 q^{Z}_{t,x}(S_{t+1}),&(S_t,A_t)=x,\\
 1,&(S_t,A_t)\ne x,
 \end{cases}
 \tag{7}
\]
and insert the initial factor \(\mathbf 1\{S_1=s_1\}\).  Finally insert, for every reward time,
\[
 \chi_t(W,S_t,A_t,S_{t+1})=
 \begin{cases}
 Hh_t^{\eta_{jb}}((S_t,A_t),S_{t+1}),&W=(j,b,t),\\
 1,&W=(j,b,\ell),\ \ell\ne t.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{8}
\]
All factors are rational and nonnegative.  Rationality follows from the theorem's input restrictions and the rational vertex construction.  Nonnegativity follows from \(R>0\), the definitions of \(m_t,M_t\), and \(\texttt{prop:affine-nonnegative-lift}\).  Equation (7) contains exactly one variable \(Z_{t,x}\) for each row; no copy is created when \(W\), the state path, or the selected reward time changes.

Fix \(z\) and sum the product of (5)--(8), the policy factors, and the initial factor over \(W\), all actions, and \(S_2,\ldots,S_{H+1}\). \[
 \begin{aligned}
 T_\sigma(z)
 &=\sum_{j=1}^H\sum_{b=0}^1\rho_{jb}
   \mathbb E_{q^z}\!\left[
    \sum_{t=1}^H h_t^{\eta_{jb}}((S_t,A_t),S_{t+1})
    \mathrel{\big|}S_1=s_1,\gamma^{jb}\right]\\
 &=\frac{1}{2C_\nu}F_i^\sigma(q^z).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{9}
\]

Multiply the current factors containing \(Z\) into \(A(Z,Y)\), where \(Y\) consists of the other uneliminated decisions in that bucket.  Legality of \(\preceq\) implies that no uneliminated chance variable occurs in \(A\).  The product of all factors outside the bucket can be written \(B(X,Y,Y')\), where \(X\) are remaining chance variables, \(Y'\) are other decisions, and \(B\) does not contain \(Z\). \[

 \tag{10}
\]

\[

 \tag{12}
\]

\[
 O\!\left(H^2N d^{w_{\mathrm c}(\preceq)+1}\right)
 \tag{13}
\]

Maximization selects one candidate rational and introduces no new denominator.  A capped simplex has at most \(|\mathcal S|2^{|\mathcal S|-1}\) vertices by the proved vertex characterization, so \(\log d\) is itself bounded by a polynomial in the explicit input length. Reverse-order backtracking fixes those later variables before consulting the stored value.  Legality removed every chance variable from a maximization bucket, so no stored choice depends on \(W\), a state, or an action realization.  Hence \(\mathsf{BP}_\sigma\) recovers one joint row assignment \(z_\sigma\), shared by all quadrature branches and all paths.

Conditional on \(E_t=1\), set the factual coordinate of \(R_t\) to \(y_t\) and draw each nonfactual coordinate from \(q^{z_\sigma}_{t,x}\). \[
 \frac{K_t(y\mid x_t)-p_t\mathbf 1\{y=y_t\}}{1-p_t}
 \tag{14}
\]

\[

 \tag{15}

Sampling these response tables independently over \(t\) gives the structural equations, transition marginals, and timewise disturbance independence required by \(\mathfrak M(K)\), in agreement with \(\texttt{lem:posterior-row-projection}\).  Equations (14)--(15) specify a conditional sampler rather than an exponential response-table mass array.

\[
 U_i(K,\tau)=R(V_{+1}-C_\nu),
 \qquad
 L_i(K,\tau)=R(C_\nu-V_{-1}).
\]
The corresponding backtracked SCMs attain the two endpoints and use one shared joint row assignment in every coalition world.  This proves all assertions.","status":"proved"}

Hence breadth-first traversal with duplicate suppression lists all vertices in \(O(|\mathcal S|^2v_{t,x})\) rational operations when this row has \(v_{t,x}\) vertices.
